subject: Re: Jan connector billing spike — request for amnesty and adjustment
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@everleaf.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: everleaf.billing@everleaf.ai
Date: 2027-02-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Discrepancy on Jan connector charges — request for adjustment

Hi Marcus / Marissa,

We pulled our January billing and noticed a large spike attributed to the connector integration (connector-prod-1). Usage looks inflated relative to our internal logs for the week of Jan 10–16. Our payroll batch ran a single test file; it shouldn't have generated the token counts you're billing for.

Could Redwood review the meter and either: 1) apply a goodwill adjustment for the excess tokens, or 2) issue a credit memo to reconcile while we investigate on our side. We're especially sensitive to VAT handling — we're VAT-registered in Ireland (IE VAT: IE1234567A) and will need evidence if you reissue invoices.

I've attached our exported usage and a short summary. Please let me know the next steps and any docs you need from us. We have an open PO (PO-10344) if that helps coordinate with finance.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Director, Platform Engineering
Everleaf.ai

Attachments: everleaf_usage_jan2027.csv (CSV, 52KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@everleaf.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-20T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Jan connector charges — request for adjustment

Thanks, Liam — we saw the usage file come through. I'm sorry for the friction here. We'll do a quick audit of the connector meter and confirm whether this was an ingestion/attribution issue or true usage.

Next steps:
- I'll loop in finance (Marissa) to prepare a provisional credit if this was an overcount.
- Jonas will check the serving logs and kernel attribution for Jan 10–16 to surface any anomalous replay or duplicated requests.
- If you can send the PO reference and any internal spike logs you have (timestamps), that'll speed validation.

Provisional ETA: initial findings by EOD tomorrow (Feb 21). If it's clearly an overcount we'll propose a credit and a plan to correct meter attribution.

Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-21T11:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Jan connector charges — request for adjustment

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the data. I've reviewed the exported usage and our preliminary meter scans. At present we see a 12,400-token delta between what your export shows and what Redwood billed (connector-prod-1, Jan 12). To move this to resolution we need the following to produce a credit memo that will hold in our accounting system:

1) Confirmation of the PO number to tie the credit to (you mentioned PO-10344).
2) Any supporting internal logs showing the test file timestamp (UTC) you referenced.
3) VAT certificate or VAT registration number for Everleaf (for EU tax reissuance).

If those are available we can generate a provisional credit memo (goodwill) while Jonas completes the technical reconciliation. Attached is a proposed calculation sheet showing the draft credit at $0.0008 per token (proposed adjustment = $9.92) and a breakdown by meter.

We can also place a temporary hold on collections for the disputed amount. Please confirm whether Everleaf prefers: A) immediate credit memo issuance and netting against next invoice, or B) a refund/offset now and invoice correction next cycle.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Finance Manager — Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_credit_calculation_8891.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)

On Feb 20, 2027, at 10:03 AM, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Liam — we saw the usage file come through...

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@everleaf.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-22T14:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Jan connector charges — request for adjustment

Liam — quick update and resolution items. After Jonas validated our logs there was a replay loop triggered by a failed acknowledgement from the connector on Jan 12; that generated duplicate token counts for a small window. We accept responsibility for the meter overcount and will issue a goodwill credit.

Resolution summary (agreed):
- One-time goodwill credit: $12,400.00 (covers the disputed period).
- Credit document: RW-CR-8891-credit-memo.pdf attached. This is provisioned as a credit memo applied to your next invoice.
- VAT handling: Because Everleaf is VAT-registered in Ireland, we'll reissue a VAT-corrected invoice if you confirm your VAT number (please reply with the exact registration string). If VAT evidence is not provided within 30 days we'll apply the credit net of VAT per our policy and follow up on tax documentation.
- Collections: we have placed a hold on the disputed amount; no collections actions will be taken while documentation is pending.

Action items for Everleaf: please confirm PO-10344 and provide the VAT registration string you want on the corrected invoice. If you want the credit paid out instead of netting against next invoice, say so and Marissa will coordinate a refund.

Thanks for the patience — apologies for the disruption. We'll also push a fix to the connector's acknowledgement handling to prevent future replays.

Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RW-CR-8891-credit-memo.pdf (PDF, 12KB)
